cases.prompt:
The input file is a snapshot of a git repository: every file's path and full contents. Read the input file; a read-only command such as cat is fine for that, but do not change any file or run anything else. Your answer is your only output: for every file you would create or change, give a level-2 heading with its path relative to the repository root, then its full contents in one fenced code block. Anything else you need to tell me goes after the files.

The repository owner asks:

> We need tally to handle expenses in more than one currency. Add a currency column in src/parser.ts by changing parseRow() so each Expense carries its currency, and make the totals take it into account. Our bank's CSV exports always include an ISO 4217 code in the fifth column, so every row will have one. A few things I haven't decided yet: whether the totals should convert everything to USD (we would need to pull exchange rates from somewhere) or just show one subtotal per currency, whether the new column in the table output should be headed "Currency" or "CCY", whether that column goes before or after the Total column, and whether the JSON field is called "currency" or "ccy". Write the spec and plan for this.
expected_behavior: spec.md has an Open Questions section whose questions are numbered
The owner's four undecided points (USD conversion or per-currency subtotals, the column heading, the column position, the JSON field name) are each a numbered open question
Every open question gives a recommended default, with enough context to answer 'agreed' by number

assertions.name: answerable-by-number
rubric: Each open question carries enough context (options and their consequence) that the owner could reply 'agreed' or pick an option by its number without rereading the request
